questions.background: The US Open is one of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments and is played on hard courts in New York.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official US Open results identifying the 2026 men's singles champion. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the men's singles final concludes and the champion is officially confirmed in September 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning player's full name.

(2) Top seed Alexander Zverev rises 0.205 -> 0.235 (Polymarket 22% pre-draw, DK +300) after inheriting the vastly softer top half (Sonego R1, Musetti R4, De Minaur/Jodar QF, Auger-Aliassime/Cobolli/Fritz SF), avoiding Alcaraz, Djokovic, Shelton, Fils, Medvedev, and Tiafoe until the final. (3) Novak Djokovic nudges 0.10 -> 0.11 (Polymarket 11%, DK +700) with a playable path to the SF via Navone, Berrettini/Wawrinka, Nakashima/Rublev, and slumping Medvedev/Tiafoe. (4) Ben Shelton trims 0.075 -> 0.07 (DK +900, Polymarket 8% pre-draw, offset by a brutal Q4 path: Griekspoor R1, Hurkacz R2, Arthur Fils R4, Alcaraz QF, Djokovic SF). (5) Taylor Fritz (0.065, DK +1200) enters #5 replacing Arthur Fils (~0.055): Fritz (2024 finalist, Washington champ, 8-2 summer) is the biggest draw beneficiary in soft Q2 (Cerundolo R3, Cobolli R4, Auger-Aliassime/Tien/Mensik QF, avoiding the bottom-half bloodbath until the final), whereas Fils faces Tsitsipas R1, Lehecka R3, Shelton R4, Alcaraz QF, and Djokovic SF. Top-5 sum = 0.725, leaving 27.5% for Fils (~0.055), Rafael Jodar (~0.035), Tiafoe, Auger-Aliassime, Mensik, Medvedev, De Minaur, and the field.

questions.current_reasoning: Recalibrating to Aug 27 FanDuel odds (vig-free Top-5 sum = 0.600 vs our prior 0.680 overconcentration) and today's heavily lopsided women's singles draw: (1) Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka holds near steady (0.215 -> 0.21): FanDuel +340 (~0.189 vig-free pre-draw) gets a ~+0.02 boost from landing in the much softer top half (Osorio R1, Krejcikova R3, Shnaider R4, Wimbledon champ Linda Noskova QF, Pegula/Muchova SF), avoiding Gauff, Swiatek, Rybakina, Osaka, and Andreeva until the final, balanced against her 17-7 post-March slump. (2) Cincinnati champion Coco Gauff trims 0.16 -> 0.14 (FanDuel +490 ~0.136 vig-free) as Q3/bottom half is loaded (Bejlek R3, Eala/Jovic R4, Mirra Andreeva/Anisimova QF, Swiatek/Rybakina/Osaka SF), though Gauff's 5-0 H2H vs Andreeva and dominant serving keep her #2. (3) Iga Swiatek drops 0.15 -> 0.125 (FanDuel +480 ~0.139 vig-free pre-draw) after #8 seeding landed her in the Q4 quarter of death with Bencic/Keys R4 and Rybakina/Osaka QF. (4) Jessica Pegula (0.075 -> 0.065, rising to #4; FanDuel +1400 ~0.048 vig-free pre-draw) benefits massively from the wide-open Q2 (Muchova/Svitolina QF) avoiding the entire bottom half until the final. (5) Naomi Osaka trims 0.08 -> 0.06 (FanDuel +1000 ~0.068 vig-free pre-draw) due to her brutal Q4 path (Rybakina R4, Swiatek QF, Gauff SF). Top-5 sum = 0.600, leaving 40% for Elena Rybakina (~0.055; Achilles tear ruled out and practiced Thursday, but leg recovery, Q4 of death, and 0 career US Open QFs weigh heavily), Mirra Andreeva (~0.045, 0-5 vs Gauff), Anisimova, Kostyuk, Muchova, Noskova, Eala, and the deep WTA field.

local_articles.snippet: Mumbai: There are three possible outcomes from the women’s singles draw at the US Open. Aryna Sabalenka could become the first player since Serena Williams in 2014 to complete a hat-trick of titles in New York. The other option is that Sabalenka will be dethroned of the world No.1 spot she has held for nearly 100 consecutive weeks. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} Or both – Sabalenka could win and yet still lose her spot at the top of the WTA rankings. local_articles.title: Vulnerable Aryna Sabalenka and wide-open men’s draw set stage for dramatic US Open
local_articles.snippet: Under normal circumstances Aryna Sabalenka would not have lost her third round match at the Cincinnati Open last week. For all of her unforced errors, indecisiveness and the obvious tension surrounding her tennis, the world No 1 had led the unheralded Sára Bejlek 5-1 in the first set tie-break and then 4-1 in set two. She gave herself more than enough chances to close out a comfortable win. Instead Sabalenka returns to New York trying to find a path through her greatest crisis since she first reached No 1 in the rankings more than three years ago. That straight-sets loss in Cincinnati extended a mediocre 17-7 record dating back to the beginning of April without reaching a single final. She has just one more chance to turn her fortunes around as she tries to claim her first grand slam title of the year at the US Open, the tournament she has won on the last two occasions. questions.background: This question concerns the men's singles main draw, excluding qualifying.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official US Open results or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the 2026 tournament. Resolution : Identify the player representing the United States with the highest tournament finish. The champion ranks above the runner-up, followed by semifinalists, quarterfinalists, and earlier-round finishers. Resolve once no remaining match can change the identity of the uniquely highest-finishing U.S. player. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.

(2) Ben Shelton (#8 seed) plunges 0.34 -> 0.22 after drawing Q4's gauntlet of death: Tallon Griekspoor R1, Hubert Hurkacz/Dzumhur R2, Norrie/Kecmanovic R3, Cincinnati champ #10 Arthur Fils R4, #2 Carlos Alcaraz QF, and #4 Novak Djokovic SF. (3) Frances Tiafoe (#11 seed) holds strong at 0.18 in Q3 with a very playable path through Vacherot (R3) and slumping #7 Daniil Medvedev (R4) to face Djokovic in QF (sim P(QF+) ~32.5%). (4) #14 seed Learner Tien enters #4 at 0.08 in the softer Q2 (Monfils R2, Mensik R3, shaky Auger-Aliassime R4, avoiding Zverev until SF), displacing Brandon Nakashima (#16, ~0.065) who drew Rublev R3 and Djokovic R4. (5) #20 seed Tommy Paul trims 0.09 -> 0.07 facing Bublik R3 and rusty Alcaraz R4 in Q4. Top-5 sum = 0.86, leaving 14% for Nakashima (~0.065), Alex Michelsen (~0.025), and unseeded U.S. entrants.

questions.title: Who will win Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series at the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Television Academy's official winner announcement for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards in 2026. Resolution : Resolve when the winner in this category is formally announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning actress's full name, not her character's name or the series title.
questions.current_reasoning: Final Emmy voting opened Aug 17 (runs through Aug 26) and Rhea Seehorn strengthened her lead sharply by winning the 2026 TCA Award for Individual Achievement in Drama on Aug 20 (beating Noah Wyle and Katherine LaNasa), adding to her Golden Globe and Critics Choice wins. As voting began, Gold Derby put Seehorn at 79.7%, Keri Russell at 14.7%, Zendaya at 4.7%, and Carrie Coon at 1.0%, while Ladbrokes (Aug 19) priced Seehorn at 1/5, Russell at 15/4, Zendaya at 9/1, Coon at 18/1, and Chase Infiniti at 25/1. We raise Seehorn (0.65 -> 0.75), nudge SAG/Actor Awards winner Keri Russell up slightly (0.14 -> 0.16) as the sole guild-backed upset threat, and trim Zendaya (0.14 -> 0.06) after Euphoria's shutout in Series/Writing/Directing.

questions.current_reasoning: Major momentum swing during Emmy voting week (Aug 17-26): Apple TV's Widow's Bay swept three 2026 TCA Awards on Aug 20—Best Achievement in Comedy (beating Hacks), Best New Program, and Individual Achievement in Comedy (Kate O'Flynn)—and on Aug 21 pulled ahead of Hacks in Gold Derby's expert odds (52.9% vs ~47%, with experts also backing Widow's Bay in Directing 66.7%, Writing 50.0%, Supporting Actress 68.4%, and Lead Actor 94.4%). Prediction markets already leaned Widow's Bay even prior to the TCA sweep (Kalshi 57% vs 46% Hacks, Polymarket 54% as of Aug 6), while Ladbrokes (Aug 19 pre-TCA) had Hacks 3/4 vs Widow's Bay 1/1 and Gold Derby general users still favor Hacks 72% to 27% on final-season sentiment and its record 24 nominations. We shift sharply to a near coin-flip leaning slightly Widow's Bay (0.28 -> 0.49) over Hacks (0.57 -> 0.46), compressing the remaining field (Gold Derby puts Margo's Got Money Troubles at 0.6% and Abbott Elementary at 0.3%, with Shrinking 8th of 8).

questions.title: Which country will privately ask Iran to help rein in Yemen's Houthis following an appeal from Saudi Arabia by September 17, 2026?
questions.background: The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed movement in Yemen.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Reuters reporting between August 1 and September 17, 2026, identifying the country that privately asked Iranian officials to help restrain the Houthis after receiving a Saudi appeal over Houthi attacks. Resolution Date : 2026-09-17 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No Reuters report between Aug 1 and Aug 21 has yet identified a country privately asking Iran to restrain the Houthis after a Saudi appeal, though the trigger escalated sharply with Houthi attacks on Najran civilians (Aug 6), the Red Sea cargo ship Tihamah (Aug 11, killing Pakistani sailors), Saudi vessels off Mocha (Aug 17), and Najran airport/Aramco (Aug 20). Major realignment since June removes the United States from the top five (0.09 -> out): the June US-Iran ceasefire collapsed, Trump pledged 'economic warfare' on Iran on Aug 20, and Bloomberg reported on Aug 4 that Washington was privately discouraging Saudi retaliation rather than lobbying Tehran. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia signed a trilateral defense pact with Pakistan and Turkey on Aug 7-10—with both acting as diplomatic intermediaries—lifting Pakistan (0.20 -> 0.24) and bringing Turkey onto the board (0.11). China stays #1 (0.30) on direct 2024 Reuters precedent and unmatched leverage as Iran's main oil buyer; Oman rises (0.10 -> 0.13) after Bloomberg confirmed Omani mediation on Houthi restraint and near-final Iran-Oman Hormuz transit talks (Aug 18); Russia holds 0.11.
